The '''51st Academy Awards''' ceremony, organized by the [[Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences]] (AMPAS), honored [[1978 in film|films released in 1978]] and took place on April 9, 1979, at the [[Dorothy Chandler Pavilion]] in Los Angeles, beginning at 7:00&nbsp;p.m. [[Pacific Time Zone|PST]] / 10:00&nbsp;p.m. [[Eastern Time Zone|EST]]. During the ceremony, AMPAS presented [[Academy Awards]] (commonly referred to as Oscars) in 21 categories. The ceremony, televised in the United States by [[American Broadcasting Company|ABC]], was produced by [[Jack Haley Jr.]] and directed by [[Marty Pasetta]].<ref>{{cite news|via=Google News Archive|title=War Film, Comedy Head List|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1338&dat=19790406&id=Mv1LAAAAIBAJ&pg=4405,1962767|work=[[The Spokesman-Review|Spokane Daily Chronicle]]|publisher=[[Cowles Publishing Company]]|date=April 6, 1979|page=7|access-date=August 24, 2015|archive-date=June 7, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220607094357/https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1338&dat=19790406&id=Mv1LAAAAIBAJ&pg=4405%2C1962767|url-status=live}}</ref> Comedian and talk show host [[Johnny Carson]] hosted the show for the first time.<ref>{{cite news |title=Frank Won't Sing Without G Notes |work=Chicago Tribune |date=October 3, 1978 |page=136}}</ref> Three days earlier, in a ceremony held at [[The Beverly Hilton]] in [[Beverly Hills, California]], the [[Academy Award for Technical Achievement|Academy Awards for Technical Achievement]] were presented by hosts [[Gregory Peck]] and [[Christopher Reeve]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Past Scientific & Technical Awards Ceremonies|url=http://www.oscars.org/awards/scitech/pastawards.html |publisher=[[Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences]] |access-date=July 31, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140213185729/http://www.oscars.org/awards/scitech/pastawards.html|archive-date=February 13, 2014}}</ref>

''[[The Deer Hunter]]'' won five awards at the main awards ceremony, including [[Academy Award for Best Picture|Best Picture]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Siskel |first1=Gene |title=Oscars to Fonda, Voight, 'Hunter' |url=http://archives.chicagotribune.com/1979/04/10/page/1/article/oscars-to-fonda-voight-hunter |work=Chicago Tribune |date=April 10, 1979 |access-date=August 24, 2015 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160308182052/http://archives.chicagotribune.com/1979/04/10/page/1/article/oscars-to-fonda-voight-hunter/ |archive-date=March 8, 2016 }}</ref> Other winners included ''[[Coming Home (1978 film)|Coming Home]]'' with three awards, ''[[Midnight Express (film)|Midnight Express]]'' with two, and ''[[The Buddy Holly Story]]'', ''[[California Suite (film)|California Suite]]'', ''[[Days of Heaven]]'', ''[[Death on the Nile (1978 film)|Death on the Nile]]'', ''[[The Flight of the Gossamer Condor]]'', ''[[Get Out Your Handkerchiefs]]'', ''[[Heaven Can Wait (1978 film)|Heaven Can Wait]]'', ''[[Scared Straight!]]'', ''[[Special Delivery (1978 film)|Special Delivery]]'', ''[[Superman (1978 film)|Superman]]'', ''[[Teenage Father]]'', and ''[[Thank God It's Friday (film)|Thank God It's Friday]]'' with one. The telecast was watched by 46.3&nbsp;million viewers and earned a 34.6 [[Nielsen ratings|Nielsen rating]] in the United States.<ref name="Viewership"/><ref name="Boca"/>

==Ceremony==
The ceremony, held at the [[Dorothy Chandler Pavilion]] in [[Downtown Los Angeles]], was hosted by late-night talk host [[Johnny Carson]] for the first time.<ref>{{cite news|via=Google News Archive|last1=Thomas|first1=Bob|title=Oscar Show-A Thankless Chore|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=110&dat=19790409&id=ItNOAAAAIBAJ&pg=6936,8014761|work=[[Ludington Daily News]]|date=April 9, 1979|access-date=August 25, 2015|archive-date=June 7, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220607094357/https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=110&dat=19790409&id=ItNOAAAAIBAJ&pg=6936%2C8014761|url-status=live}}</ref> [[Jack Elliott (composer)|Jack Elliott]] and [[Allyn Ferguson]] served as musical directors for the telecast.<ref>{{harvnb|Osborne|2013|p=413}}</ref> Singers [[Sammy Davis Jr.]] and [[Steve Lawrence]] performed a medley called "Oscar's Only Human," which was composed of movie songs that were not nominated for Best Original Song.<ref>{{harvnb|Wiley|Bona|1996|p=560}}</ref> Initially, the academy's music branch protested the segment and urged that it be dropped from the ceremony, but it was kept after Haley threatened to leave his position as producer and pull Carson from emcee duties.<ref>{{harvnb|Pond|2005|p=29}}</ref>

It is also remembered for being the final public appearance of Oscar-winning actor [[John Wayne]], where he was given a standing ovation before presenting the award for [[Academy Award for Best Picture|Best Picture]].<ref name="NMO">{{harvnb|Osborne|2013|p=251}}</ref> On June 11, two months after the ceremony, he died from complications from [[stomach cancer]] at age 72.<ref name="NMO"/><ref>{{cite news |last1=Hammond |first1=Pete |title=How Michael Cimino's 'The Deer Hunter' Pioneered The Modern Day Oscar Campaign – And Won |url=https://deadline.com/2016/07/michael-ciminos-deer-hunter-oscar-campaign-win-best-picture-1201782549/ |access-date=February 19, 2021 |work=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |date=July 3, 2016 |archive-date=April 17, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200417162635/https://deadline.com/2016/07/michael-ciminos-deer-hunter-oscar-campaign-win-best-picture-1201782549/ |url-status=live }}</ref>  This was also the final public appearance for [[Jack Haley]], the father of producer [[Jack Haley Jr.]], who presented the [[Academy Award for Best Costume Design|Best Costume Design]] with his ''[[Wizard of Oz (1939 film)|Wizard of Oz]]'' co-star [[Ray Bolger]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Smith |first1=J.Y. |title=Jack Haley Dies, Was Tin Man in 'The Wizard of Oz' |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/local/1979/06/07/jack-haley-dies-was-tin-man-in-the-wizard-of-oz/2c6b95f4-2ec3-49a5-bf62-4b09596f6642/ |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |date=June 7, 1979 |access-date=October 31, 2020 |url-access=subscription |archive-date=April 1, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190401114319/https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/local/1979/06/07/jack-haley-dies-was-tin-man-in-the-wizard-of-oz/2c6b95f4-2ec3-49a5-bf62-4b09596f6642/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Winners and nominees==
The nominees for the 51st Academy Awards were announced on February 20, 1979, by Academy president [[Howard W. Koch]] and actress [[Susan Blakely]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Thomas |first1=Bob |title=1978 Oscar nominees announced |work=[[San Bernardino Sun]] |date=February 21, 1979 |page=C1}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=The Deer Hunter, Heaven Can Wait top honors Oscar nominees listed|work=[[The Globe and Mail]]|date=February 21, 1979|page=P11}}</ref> ''[[The Deer Hunter]]'' and ''[[Heaven Can Wait (1978 film)|Heaven Can Wait]]'' tied for the most nominations with nine each.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Grant|first1=Lee|title=Two War Films on Oscar Ballot|work=[[Los Angeles Times]] |date=February 21, 1979|page=D1}}</ref> The winners were announced during the awards ceremony on April 9.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Harmetz |first1=Aljean |title=2 Vietnam Films Cast Aside Ghosts on Way to Oscars |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1979/04/11/archives/2-vietnam-films-cast-aside-ghosts-on-way-to-oscars-new-york.html |access-date=November 12, 2020 |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=April 11, 1979 |url-access=subscription |archive-date=November 12, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201112215758/https://www.nytimes.com/1979/04/11/archives/2-vietnam-films-cast-aside-ghosts-on-way-to-oscars-new-york.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Best Director nominees [[Warren Beatty]] and [[Buck Henry]] became the second pair of directors nominated in that category for the same film; [[Jerome Robbins]] and [[Robert Wise]] had won for co-directing 1961's ''[[West Side Story (1961 film)|West Side Story]]''.<ref>{{harvnb|Kinn|Piazza|2002|p=215}}</ref> Furthermore, Beatty was the first person to earn acting, directing, producing, and screenwriting nominations for the same film. While [[Orson Welles]] had previously achieved the same feat for ''[[Citizen Kane]]'', rules at the time determined that the studio releasing the film, as opposed to the individual producers, were the official nominees for Best Picture.<ref>{{harvnb|Wiley|Bona|1996|p=1129}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Emerson |first1=Jim |title=Questions for the Academy |url=https://www.rogerebert.com/scanners/questions-for-the-academy |access-date=March 21, 2016 |work=[[Chicago Sun-Times]] |date=February 11, 2007 |archive-date=March 13, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170313185720/http://www.rogerebert.com/scanners/questions-for-the-academy |url-status=live }}</ref> With [[Jon Voight]] and [[Jane Fonda]]'s respective wins in the Best Actor and Best Actress categories, ''[[Coming Home (1978 film)|Coming Home]]'' was the fourth film to win both lead acting awards.<ref name="Osborne 2013 423">{{harvnb|Osborne|2013|p=423}}</ref> Best Supporting Actress winner [[Maggie Smith]] became the only person to win an Oscar for playing an Oscar loser in ''[[California Suite (film)|California Suite]]''.<ref name="Osborne 2013 423"/>

===Special Achievement Award (Visual Effects)===
* ''[[Superman (1978 film)|Superman]]'' – [[Les Bowie]], [[Colin Chilvers]], [[Denys Coop]], [[Roy Field]], [[Derek Meddings]] and [[Zoran Perisic (visual effects artist)|Zoran Perisic]].<ref>{{harvnb|Franks|2005|p=246}}</ref>

===Honorary Awards===
* To [[Walter Lantz]] for bringing joy and laughter to every part of the world through his unique animated motion pictures.<ref>{{cite news |title=Animator Walter Lantz, Creator of Woody Woodpecker, Is Dead |url=https://buffalonews.com/news/animator-walter-lantz-creator-of-woody-woodpecker-is-dead/article_fa67a64c-ab42-5f22-9a5c-5d80f6639891.html |access-date=July 16, 2020 |work=[[The Buffalo News]] |date=March 23, 1994 |url-access=limited |archive-date=July 17, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200717150743/https://buffalonews.com/news/animator-walter-lantz-creator-of-woody-woodpecker-is-dead/article_fa67a64c-ab42-5f22-9a5c-5d80f6639891.html |url-status=live }}</ref>
* To [[Museum of Modern Art Department of Film|The Museum of Modern Art Department of Film]] for the contribution it has made to the public's perception of movies as an art form.<ref>{{harvnb|Kinn|Piazza|2002|p=217}}</ref>
* To [[Laurence Olivier]] for the full body of his work, for the unique achievements of his entire career and his lifetime of contribution to the art of film.<ref name="HonoraryandSpecial">{{cite web |title=Academy Awards Acceptance Speech Database |url=http://aaspeechesdb.oscars.org/results.aspx?QY=find%20(year%20term%20ct%201978)&AC=QBE_QUERY&RF=WebReportList&DF=WebReportOscars&MR=0&BU=/index.aspx |publisher=Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences (AMPAS) |access-date=February 4, 2020 |archive-date=July 16, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200716052025/http://aaspeechesdb.oscars.org/results.aspx?QY=find%20%28year%20term%20ct%201978%29&AC=QBE_QUERY&RF=WebReportList&DF=WebReportOscars&MR=0&BU=%2Findex.aspx |url-status=live }}</ref>
* To [[King Vidor]] for his incomparable achievements as a cinematic creator and innovator.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Thomas |first1=David |title=The Man Who Would Be King |url=https://www.dga.org/craft/dgaq/all-articles/1004-winter-2010-11/interview-king-vidor.aspx |access-date=July 16, 2020 |work=[[DGA Quarterly]] |date=Winter 2011 |archive-date=May 20, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200520212536/https://www.dga.org/Craft/DGAQ/All-Articles/1004-Winter-2010-11/Interview-King-Vidor.aspx |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Jean Hersholt Humanitarian Award===
The award recognizes individuals whose humanitarian efforts have brought credit to the motion picture industry.<ref>{{cite web |title=Jean Hersholt Humanitarian Award |url=https://www.oscars.org/governors/hersholt |publisher=Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences |access-date=12 November 2020 |archive-date=16 November 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201116224625/https://www.oscars.org/governors/hersholt |url-status=live }}</ref>
* [[Leo Jaffe]]<ref>{{cite news|last1=Schreger|first1=Charles|title='Close Encounters' - Take Two|work=Los Angeles Times |date=February 10, 1979|page=B5}}</ref>
